title: URL shortener with base-62 codes and click statistics
prompt:
Build a URL shortener in Python.

Modules:
- codec.py:
  - `encode_base62(n: int) -> str` encodes a non-negative integer using the alphabet `0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ` (so 0 -> `"0"`, 61 -> `"Z"`, 62 -> `"10"`). Raises `ValueError` for negative numbers.
  - `decode_base62(s: str) -> int` reverses it. Raises `ValueError` for an empty string or any character outside the alphabet.
- shortener.py: `class Shortener`.
  - `shorten(url) -> str` returns a short code. Raises `ValueError` unless the url starts with `http://` or `https://`. Codes are `encode_base62` of a counter that starts at 1 and increases with each new URL. Shortening a URL that was already shortened returns its existing code (and does not use a new number).
  - `expand(code) -> str` returns the original URL and counts one click; raises `KeyError` for an unknown code.
  - `clicks(code) -> int` returns how many times that code has been expanded; raises `KeyError` for an unknown code.
- main.py: command-line interface. Read commands from standard input, one per line, until `quit` or end of input:
  - `shorten <url>` prints the code
  - `expand <code>` prints the URL
  - `clicks <code>` prints the number of clicks
  - On any error print a line starting with `Error:` and continue.

Constraints: use only the Python standard library. The entry point is main.py in the project root, guarded by `if __name__ == "__main__":`.
